content: The FAM107B gene is a genetic sequence found in humans. It is located on the minus strand of chromosome 10, specifically at the p13 region, which corresponds to the short arm of the chromosome. This gene is also known by several alternative names, including C10orf45, FLJ45505, MGC11034, and MGC90261. Within the FAM107B gene, there is a conserved domain called DUF1151, which belongs to a family of eukaryotic proteins with currently unknown functions. The FAM107B gene is expressed in most human tissues, but its expression does not show a high frequency in any specific tissue. It is also expressed throughout all stages of human development. The mRNA transcript of FAM107B is 3,785 base pairs in length and contains five exons. The protein encoded by this gene is referred to as LOC83641 and is composed of 306 amino acids. According to AceView, there are 27 spliced variants and 2 unspliced variants of FAM107B, resulting in 27 mRNA transcripts. Of these, only 23 spliced and unspliced mRNA variants are known to encode high-quality proteins. Additionally, there are 17 distinct isoforms of the protein. FAM107B does not function as a signal peptide but is believed to be a protein exported to the mitochondria. The gene is located in a genomic neighborhood that includes other genes such as FRMD4A (FERM domain-containing 4A), LOC100289125 (a hypothetical protein), RPSAP7 (ribosomal protein SA pseudogene 7), CDNF (cerebral dopamine neurotrophic factor), and HSPA14. FAM107B has one paralog, FAM107A, and numerous orthologs in other organisms, including primates, dogs, cows, mice, and chickens. These orthologs exhibit a high degree of conservation across species. Structurally, two proteins share significant similarity with FAM107B. One is a human septin trimer, which belongs to the Ras-like GTPase superfamily. Members of this superfamily are involved in regulating cytoskeletal reorganization, gene expression, vesicle trafficking, nucleocytoplasmic transport, and microtubule organization. The other is the third HMG-box of mouse UBF1, which is part of the HMG-box superfamily. Proteins in this family bind to DNA, causing it to bend or distort, which can result in the looping of linear DNA, the formation of four-way DNA junctions, and the creation of DNA bulges. Some members of this family also include mitochondrial transcription factors that bind at four-way DNA junctions. Several proteins are known to interact with the FAM107B protein. These include: Autophagy-related proteins involved in cytoplasmic-to-vacuole transport, specifically in the formation of Cvt vesicles. A probable protein kinase, which is a heat shock-like protein and an antigen. A kinesin-related protein, which is a biliary glycoprotein isoantigen. A hypothetical protein, HP0231, which functions as a somatostatin receptor. ISWI complex protein 2, a mitochondrial reverse transcriptase-like protein. CG7077-PA, an open reading frame protein associated with Alu repetitive sequences. Model organisms have been utilized to study the function of FAM107B. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Fam107btm1a(KOMP)Wtsi, was created as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This program aims to generate and distribute animal models of disease for research purposes. Male and female mice underwent a standardized phenotypic screening to assess the effects of gene deletion. A total of 26 tests were conducted on the mutant mice, and two significant abnormalities were identified. Homozygous animals exhibited abnormal brainstem auditory evoked potentials and increased trabecular bone thickness.
